dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:4101.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 少 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4102.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 臣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4103.text: A place in Song. Formed from 邑, with 毚 indicating the sound. Read like 讒.

shuowen:4104.text: A place between Song and Lu. Formed from 邑, with 晉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4105.text: The state enfeoffed to a son of King Wen of Zhou. Formed from 邑, with 告 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4106.text: A place in Wei, now Juancheng in Jiyin. Formed from 邑, with 垔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4107.text: Qiong territory, in Jiyin County. Formed from 邑, with 工 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4108.text: The fief of Zhurong’s descendants of the Yun surname, between the Zhen and Wei rivers. Zheng destroyed it. Formed from 邑, with 會 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4109.text: A Zheng settlement. Formed from 邑, with 元 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4110.text: A place in Zheng. Formed from 邑, with 延 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4111.text: A Ju settlement in Langya. Formed from 邑, with 更 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Capture Geng.”

shuowen:4112.text: A state of the Yun surname. Formed from 邑, with 禹 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “The people of Yu worked their rice fields.” Read like 榘 in 規榘.

shuowen:4113.text: A county in Lu, the ancient state of Zhu, enfeoffed to Emperor Zhuanxu’s descendants. Formed from 邑, with 芻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4114.text: A lower settlement of Zhu. Formed from 邑, with 余 indicating the sound. East of Lu is 䣄 City. Read like 塗.

shuowen:4115.text: A dependent state at Shi Pavilion in Kangfu, Dongping. Formed from 邑, with 寺 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Capture Shi.”

shuowen:4116.text: A lower settlement of Lu, Confucius’s home township. Formed from 邑, with 取 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4117.text: A settlement of Lu’s Meng clan. Formed from 邑, with 成 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4118.text: The state of 䣍, punished by the Duke of Zhou, in Lu. Formed from 邑, with 奄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4119.text: A lower settlement of Lu. Formed from 邑, with 雚 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “The men of Qi came to return Huan.”

shuowen:4120.text: A pavilion in Lu. Formed from 邑, with 良 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4121.text: The state enfeoffed to Zhonghui, Tang’s left minister and a descendant of Xizhong, in Xue County, 辥, Lu. Formed from 邑, with 丕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4122.text: A Ji settlement. Formed from 邑, with 章 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4123.text: A state now belonging to Linhuai. Formed from 邑, with 干 indicating the sound. Another explanation: Han originally belonged to Wu.

shuowen:4124.text: A place in Xu, Linhuai. Formed from 邑, with 義 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Xu 䣡 Chu”; the wording is uncertain.

shuowen:4125.text: A township in Wuyan, Dongping. Formed from 邑, with 后 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4126.text: A county in Donghai, enfeoffed to Emperor Shaohao’s descendants. Formed from 邑, with 炎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4127.text: A county in Donghai, formerly a settlement of the Marquis of Ji. Formed from 邑, with 吾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4128.text: A settlement in Donghai. Formed from 邑, with 巂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4129.text: A state of the Si surname, in Donghai. Formed from 邑, with 曾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4130.text: Langya Commandery, 琅邪. Formed from 邑, with 牙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4131.text: A county in Langya, also called Chunde. Formed from 邑, with 夫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4132.text: A place in Qi. Formed from 邑, with 桼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4133.text: The ruins of Qi’s Guo clan. They approved of good men but could not promote them, and hated evil men but could not remove them; thus their state perished. Formed from 邑, with 𩫏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4134.text: A place in Qi. Formed from 邑, with 兒 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Gao Hou of Qi settled the fields of Ni.”

shuowen:4135.text: Bohai territory, 郣海. Formed from 邑, with 孛 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a rise in the ground is 郣.

shuowen:4136.text: A state destroyed by Duke Huan of Qi. Formed from 邑, with 覃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4137.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 句 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4138.text: A township in Chenliu. Formed from 邑, with 亥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4139.text: A former state in Chenliu. Formed from 邑, with 𢦔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4140.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 燕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4141.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 丘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4142.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 如 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4143.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 丑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4144.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 几 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4145.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 翕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4146.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 求 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4147.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 嬰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4148.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 尚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4149.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 并 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4150.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 虖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4151.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 火 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4152.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 翏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4153.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 爲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4154.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 屯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4155.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 舍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4156.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 盍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4157.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 乾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4158.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 𤎭 indicating the sound. Read like 淫.

shuowen:4159.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 山 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4160.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 㙶 indicating the sound; 㙶 is the ancient graph 堂.

shuowen:4161.text: A state of the Ji surname. Formed from 邑, with 馮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4162.text: A township in Anyang, Runan. Formed from 邑, with abbreviated 𦳋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4163.text: A pavilion in Shangcai, Runan. Formed from 邑, with 甫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4164.text: A county in Nanyang. Formed from 邑, with 麗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4165.text: A place name. Formed from 邑, with 𠨧 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4166.text: Formed from reversed 邑. The graph 𨛜 follows this. Further explanation is missing.

shuowen:4167.text: A neighborhood road. Formed from 邑 and 𨙨. All characters in this group are formed from 𨛜. Further explanation is missing. The present clerical transformation is 𨙵.

shuowen:4168.text: Outlying settlements of a state, the townships where people are allotted land. Agricultural officers administer them separately. Within the boundary are six townships, administered as six townships. Formed from 𨛜, with 皀 indicating the sound; the administrative wording is uncertain.

shuowen:4169.text: A road within a neighborhood. Formed from 𨛜 and 共: something shared by all within the settlement.

shuowen:4170.text: Fullness: the essence of the great yang does not diminish. Formed from 囗 and 一; pictographic. All characters in this group are formed from 日.

shuowen:4171.text: The autumn sky. Formed from 日, with 文 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: “When benevolently covering those below with compassion, it is called 旻天.”

shuowen:4172.text: The four seasons. Formed from 日, with 寺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4173.text: Morning. Formed from 日 above 甲.

shuowen:4174.text: Still dark. Formed from 日, with 勿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4175.text: 昧爽, the light of dawn. Formed from 日, with 未 indicating the sound. Another explanation: dark.

shuowen:4176.text: The light of dawn. Formed from 日, with 者 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4177.text: 昭晣, bright. Formed from 日, with 折 indicating the sound. The Rites says: “Conduct affairs when light has dawned.”

shuowen:4178.text: The sun’s brightness. Formed from 日, with 召 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4179.text: Bright. Formed from 日, with 吾 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Awake, beating the breast” (晤辟有摽); interpretation of the recorded quotation is uncertain.

shuowen:4180.text: Bright. Formed from 日, with 勺 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “It is a white-marked forehead.”

shuowen:4181.text: Bright. Formed from 日, with 光 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4182.text: Bright. Formed from 日, with 廣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4183.text: The appearance of the sun rising at dawn. Formed from 日, with 九 indicating the sound. Read like 勖. Another explanation: bright.

shuowen:4184.text: To advance. When the sun rises, all things advance. Formed from 日 and 臸. The Changes says: “Brightness emerges above the earth: 㬜.”

shuowen:4185.text: The sun rising. Formed from 日, with 昜 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: “Sunrise Valley.”

shuowen:4186.text: The sky clearing by day after rain. Formed from 日, with abbreviated 啓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4187.text: The sun briefly appearing through covering clouds. Formed from 日, with 易 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4188.text: Warmth from the rising sun. Formed from 日, with 句 indicating the sound. Beidi has Xuyan County, 昫衍.

shuowen:4189.text: The sun appearing. Formed from 日 and 見; 見 also indicates the sound. The Odes says: “When sunlight appears, it melts.”

shuowen:4190.text: The sky clear. Formed from 日, with 安 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4191.text: Stars visible without clouds. Formed from 日, with 燕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4192.text: Light. Formed from 日, with 京 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4193.text: The appearance of the rising sun. Formed from 日, with 告 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4194.text: 晧旰, bright. Formed from 日, with 臯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4195.text: Light. Formed from 日 and 𠌶.

shuowen:4196.text: Light. Formed from 日, with 軍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4197.text: Late in the day. Formed from 日, with 干 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “The day is late and the ruler is weary.”

shuowen:4198.text: The sun moving slowly, 暆暆. Formed from 日, with 施 indicating the sound. Lelang has Dongyi County, 東暆. Read like 酏.

shuowen:4199.text: The sun’s shadow. Formed from 日, with 咎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4200.text: When the sun is in the west: slanting. Formed from 日, with 仄 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “The slanting sun’s brightness.”
